questions.stem: To fully describe a rotation, you need to state three things. Which is NOT one of them?

options.text: The direction of rotation (clockwise or anticlockwise)

questions.explanation: A rotation is described by the centre, angle, and direction. Scale factor is used for enlargements, not rotations.

questions.stem: A point $(3, 1)$ is rotated $90°$ clockwise about the origin. What are the new coordinates?
questions.explanation: For a $90°$ clockwise rotation about the origin, the rule is $(x, y) \to (y, -x)$. So $(3, 1) \to (1, -3)$.

questions.stem: After any rotation, which of the following is true?

options.text: The shape is congruent to the original
Every point stays the same distance from the mirror line

questions.explanation: Rotations preserve size and shape, so the image is always congruent to the original. Orientation is preserved (not reversed).

questions.stem: A rotation of $180°$ about the origin maps $(2, -5)$ to which point?
questions.explanation: A $180°$ rotation about the origin maps $(x, y)$ to $(-x, -y)$. So $(2, -5)$ becomes $(-2, 5)$.

questions.stem: Which point does NOT move during a rotation?

options.text: The point furthest from the centre
Every point moves during a rotation

questions.explanation: The centre of rotation is the fixed point that does not move. All other points rotate around it.

questions.stem: A $90°$ anticlockwise rotation is equivalent to which clockwise rotation?
questions.explanation: A $90°$ anticlockwise rotation is the same as a $360° - 90° = 270°$ clockwise rotation.

questions.stem: After a rotation, each point on the shape is the same distance from the centre of rotation as it was before. This is because:

options.text: The shape has been enlarged by scale factor 1
Points move along circular arcs centred on the centre of rotation
The shape has been reflected twice
The translation vector has length zero

questions.explanation: During a rotation, every point traces a circular arc around the centre of rotation, keeping its distance from the centre constant.
